operations.title: Check a build sheet, alone or against its FBX
operations.summary: Check a build sheet: alone, or against its delivery (the FBX or GLB), naming each problem's cell and fix; optionally write the take list the artist builds from.

sheet.description: The sheet (CSV path or URL); empty where *settings* names it.

delivery.description: The delivery's FBX or GLB; empty checks the sheet alone.

mapping.description: The template's name (`interactive`, `linear`, `default` or a user's).

takes.description: Where to write the take list (CSV); empty writes none.

settings.description: A sheet settings file (`SheetSettings`): its sheet, delivery, template, names, clause templates and retired IDs, in place of *sheet*, *delivery* and *mapping*.

operations.title: Rewrite an old build sheet in the Interactive format
operations.summary: Rewrite *sheet* in the format *to* at *out*, from what its tolerant reading against *delivery* bound.

sheet.description: The old sheet (CSV path or URL); empty where *settings* names it.

delivery.description: Its delivery's FBX or GLB; empty where *settings* names it.

mapping.description: The old sheet's template (`default`: the tolerant reading).

settings.description: The old sheet's settings file (`SheetSettings`): its sheet, delivery (extra files too), template, options, renamed nodes and clause templates, in place of *sheet*, *delivery*, *mapping* and *options*.

to.description: The format to write: a template whose reading lists its columns (`interactive`, `linear`).

cells.description: Write the format's cells (a step's own row, then a row per action with its word and its names: the reading's `cell_columns`); False writes the older sheet of sentences.

operations.title: Read a sheet again and stage its plan and delivery into a Unity project
operations.summary: Read a sheet again and stage its plan, its delivery and its steps' files into a Unity project.

project.description: The Unity project's folder (the one holding `Assets`).

folder.description: Where to stage, under the project (`Assets/...`); empty: `Assets/<settings stem>`.

operations.title: Compile the package's C#
operations.summary: Compile every assembly under *source*, editor and player builds, without the optional packages and (given a reference project) with them.

source.description: The folder holding the package's `.asmdef` files; default: this checkout's own package (`com.m3trik.unitytk/`).

editor.description: The editor whose compiler and assemblies to use: a Unity executable or an installed version (`"6000.3.10f1"`); default: the newest installed.

reference_project.description: A project an editor imported with the URP, Input System and XR Interaction Toolkit packages, whose `Library/ScriptAssemblies` the package half compiles against; default, for the package itself (no *source*): the owned project of *editor* once imported; without one, only the half without them is built.

tests.description: Compile the package's test assemblies too, in the editor build with the packages, where the reference project holds the Test Framework (they are Editor-only and need its assemblies and NUnit); False leaves them out, a faster loop that cannot see a broken test file.

operations.title: Build the owned test and demo project
operations.summary: Build the owned project for *editor* (the newest when `None`) and *pipeline*, or refresh it: made once by Unity's CLI from the editor's template, its manifest naming this checkout's package every time.

key.description: Another project of its own beside the owned one (`folder`), built and refreshed alike: a run that must not share the owned project builds its own.

replacements.description: Per sample, a folder of files delivered in place of its own (`import_samples`).

muted.description: Mute it (`mute`) or let it sound; `None` mutes the owned project, which tests and agent sessions run unattended, and leaves a keyed one (a person's play project) as it is.

tuned.description: Tune its pipeline assets (`tune_pipeline`) or leave them as its template made them; `None` tunes the owned project and leaves a keyed one's as they are. Its renderers keep the template's settings either way: what a delivery needs of them, the package's own checks name (`LightmapsActions .Validate`), as they do in a person's project.

operations.title: Install unitytk in a Unity project
operations.summary: Install unitytk's package in *project*: one line in its manifest.
